blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: We present TextSeal2, a distortion-free watermark for large language models that keeps its signal under speculative decoding: tokens that replace rejected drafts remain watermarked with the same keys, and the acceptance rate is unchanged. It also preserves output diversity and adds no measurable inference latency. Its predecessor, TextSeal, restores diversity in the Gumbel-max scheme by routing each token to one of two keys via a coin flip. This is suboptimal because the detector averages the scores from both keys without knowing which key was used. TextSeal2 instead merges two or more keys into a single virtual key and couples it to fresh noise through AutoMark's Gaussian copula. Any number of keys, including publicly shared keys, can be merged this way without diluting detection. Under speculative decoding, TextSeal2 verifies keyed drafts with one more exponential race, run on the leftovers of the draft races. By memorylessness, this race reproduces block verification, so the output follows the target model exactly. We evaluate TextSeal2 on three LLMs. At equal output token diversity, TextSeal2 detects 8 to 22 percentage points more 100-token answers than TextSeal at a false-positive rate of $10^{-3}$, and is comparable to textGrain while requiring no post-logits optimization. Under speculative decoding, it detects 18 and 22 percentage points more 200-token answers than TextSeal and textGrain, respectively, at the same acceptance rate.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Identifying AI-generated text helps prevent misuse, from fabricated news ( Zellers et al., 2019 ; Crothers et al., 2022 ) to model distillation by malicious actors ( Sander et al., 2024 ) .
An LLM watermark embeds a keyed statistical signal at generation time: each token is sampled from the model’s next-token distribution through a coupling with pseudo-random values derived from a secret key and the preceding tokens.
The detector recomputes these values from the key and the text and tests whether the tokens are statistically aligned with them.
The EU AI Act requires providers to mark AI-generated content ( European Union, 2024 ) , and watermarking is deployed at scale: SynthID-Text runs in Gemini ( Dathathri et al., 2024 ) , Anthropic marks Claude outputs ( Anthropic, 2026 ) , OpenAI deploys textGrain ( Li et al., 2026 ) , and we released TextSeal ( Sander et al., 2026 ) .

LLM 水印在生成时嵌入了密钥统计信号:每个信使通过与从密钥和上个信使所衍生出伪随机值的耦合,从模型的相邻分布中取出样本.

blocks.en:
We argue that a deployed watermark should meet four requirements: it should (i) preserve the model’s output distribution; (ii) keep answers diverse under a fixed watermark key; (iii) add minimal latency to decoding;
and (iv) preserve the acceptance rate of speculative decoding ( Leviathan et al., 2023 ; Chen et al., 2023 ; Sun et al., 2025 ) .
Schemes whose next-token distribution, averaged over all possible keys, equals the model’s are called distortion-free .
The earliest such scheme applies the Gumbel-max trick to keyed pseudo-random values ( Aaronson and Kirchner, 2023 ) ; later ones achieve the same property with other samplers ( Christ et al., 2023 ; Hu et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2023 ; Kuditipudi et al., 2023 ) .
Distortionary schemes such as the green list ( Kirchenbauer et al., 2023 ) instead shift token probabilities, trading quality for detectability; we focus on distortion-free schemes.

blocks.en:
Every distortion-free watermark couples the sampled token to key-derived randomness ( Li et al., 2025 ; Xie et al., 2025 ; Long et al., 2025 ; Tsur et al., 2025 ; He et al., 2025 ; Gloaguen et al., 2026 ) .
If the key fully determines the token, detection is strongest but repeated generations with the same context never vary; if the token is independent of the key, sampling is unchanged but carries no signal.
Put differently, watermarking removes a fraction of each token’s entropy, which is the budget formulation of textGrain ( Li et al., 2026 ) .
Schemes differ in how they trade diversity against detectability.
TextSeal routes each token to one of two keys by a coin flip ( Sander et al., 2026 ) ; textGrain samples from a regularized optimal-transport coupling solved at every decoding step ( Li et al., 2026 ) ; SynthID-Text selects among randomly sampled candidates by tournament ( Dathathri et al., 2024 ) ; and AutoMark blends its Gumbel values with freshly drawn noise through a Gaussian copula ( Gloaguen et al., 2026 ) .
Other couplings rely on reweighting ( Hu et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2023 ) , inverse-transform sampling ( Kuditipudi et al., 2023 ) , or maximal couplings ( Xie et al., 2025 ; Long et al., 2025 ; Tsur et al., 2025 ) .
Dual-key constructions such as TextSeal also support tampering detection ( Feng et al., 2026 ) and public detection, with one key public and the other private ( Milis et al., 2026 ) .
Among these, textGrain detects the most watermarked text at a given diversity, but its optimal transport adds post-logits latency and its speculative variant lowers acceptance, violating our requirements (iii) and (iv) presented above.

blocks.en:
We present TextSeal2, which retains TextSeal’s two keys, meets all four requirements, and matches the state of the art in detectability.
Our starting point is a diagnosis of the gap between TextSeal, textGrain, and AutoMark.
In TextSeal, each token is generated under one key, but the detector does not know which key, and must average the scores from both keys.
This halves the signal and reduces the signal-to-noise ratio by 2 \sqrt{2} .
AutoMark and textGrain do not suffer from this loss because they use a single key, which the detector scores on every token, and draw their diversity from fresh randomness.

在"TextSeal"中,每个令牌都是在一个密钥下生成的,但探测器不知道哪个密钥,必须从两个密钥中平均得分.
这将信号减半,并将信号对噪比降低2\sqrt{2}.
AutoMark和textGrain不会因此受损失,因为他们使用一个单一的密钥,探测器在每个符上都得分,并从新鲜的随机性中汲取出他们的多样性.

blocks.en:
TextSeal2 makes three contributions to reach the state of the art ( Table 1 , Figure 1 ): • Copula mixing ( subsection 3.1 ).
We merge the two keys’ Gaussian values into a single virtual key and apply AutoMark’s copula on it.
Each key retains its role (e.g., one can be published to allow for public detection), and additional keys can be merged without diluting detection. • The residual race for speculative decoding ( subsection 3.2 ).
Gumbel-max sampling, used for the keyed drafts, is an exponential race.
By memorylessness, the losers’ leftovers are fresh exponentials.
We use this property to run one more race on them, and with block verification ( Sun et al., 2025 ) , we decide the first draft token to be rejected, and the bonus token.
The output is exactly distortion-free, acceptance is that of block verification ( Proposition 1 ), and detection gains 28 to 33 percentage points over drawing the last token of each round under an independent key. • A calibrated strength parameter ( subsection 3.3 ).
The coupling strength ρ \rho plays the role of textGrain’s entropy budget β \beta : the entropy it removes from a token of positive entropy increases strictly with ρ \rho ( Theorem 1 ).
No distortion-free scheme can obtain more detection evidence per token than the entropy it removes, and the copula comes close to this bound ( Proposition 3 ).

A sampler is single-token distortion-free if, in expectation over the key, every token retains its model probability given the prefix ( Dathathri et al., 2024 ) .
It is single-sequence distortion-free if the distribution of the entire answer is likewise preserved.
Windows repeat often in code and long reasoning traces.
Reusing a window’s keyed values re-runs the same race, so the text is single-token but not single-sequence distortion-free.
Repeated context masking draws fresh values at the later occurrences of a window, i.e. plain sampling there ( Dathathri et al., 2024 ) .
AutoMark’s ResidualRace instead continues the window’s race from its leftovers ( Gloaguen et al., 2026 ) .
Both make the text single-sequence distortion-free (Appendix A.5 ).
At detection, each (window, token) pair is scored once, to avoid biasing the detection test ( Fernandez et al., 2023 ) .

At each decoding step, it uses the key and the window to partition the vocabulary into B B blocks and to draw a B × m B\times m table of keyed Gumbel costs. Sinkhorn iterations then solve an entropy-regularised optimal-transport problem between the block probabilities and m m columns, calibrated so that the key removes a prescribed fraction β \beta of the token’s entropy; a keyed column is selected, and the block and token are sampled from the resulting coupling with freshly drawn randomness.
Only the key-only computations can overlap the model’s forward pass: the Sinkhorn iterations require the next-token distribution, and the following step requires the sampled token, so this work lies on the critical path of decoding. Better kernels can shorten it but not remove it (1–3 ms per token in our implementation, 0.2–0.4 ms in a minimal version; Appendix D ).

blocks.en:
Speculative decoding poses a specific problem for watermarking: the token that verification emits after the kept drafts must follow a residual distribution, such as ( 3 ), and must itself carry the watermark.
Prior approaches each give up something.
Re-running the race with weights r → \vec{r} on the same keyed values distorts the output, because the draft’s win shifts the remaining values ( Remark 1 ).
Replacing from fresh noise ( Hu and Huang, 2024 ) or from a second key ( Sander et al., 2026 ; Dathathri et al., 2024 ) keeps the acceptance rate, but the replaced tokens, about a third of the text in our experiments, then lose the watermark or split it across keys.
Verifying between the watermarked distributions keeps the watermark but accepts fewer drafts ( Hu and Huang, 2024 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Dathathri et al., 2024 ) ( Proposition 2 ). He et al. (2026) let the detector guess which key made each token, and Liu et al. (2026) use several drafts per position.
TextSeal2 keeps both the keys and the acceptance of block verification, with two races on the same keyed values.

This proposition says that the residual race preserves the output distribution and the acceptance of block verification.

Under a fixed key, the diversity that remains is exactly the entropy the key does not remove: whatever randomness the independent noise still contributes.
textGrain calibrates its strength directly in these terms, removing a prescribed fraction β \beta of each token’s entropy ( Li et al., 2026 ) .
In TextSeal2, the coupling strength ρ \rho plays the same role.
For a token of positive entropy, the entropy removed is a strictly increasing function of ρ \rho , from none at ρ = 0 \rho=0 to the token’s full entropy at ρ = 1 \rho=1 ( Theorem 1 ), so any target budget can be met by a unique ρ \rho , token by token if desired.
In practice this calibration is unnecessary: a fixed ρ \rho removes nearly the same fraction of a token’s entropy – ρ ≈ 0.64 \rho\approx 0.64 , 0.81 0.81 and 0.93 0.93 remove about 30%, 50% and 70% respectively, across a range of many-token distribution shapes ( Appendix C ).
We therefore use a single constant ρ \rho throughout, with a per-token ρ t \rho_{t} available when an exact budget guarantee is required.

blocks.en:
Detection is the fraction of watermarked answers declared watermarked at a nominal false-positive rate of 10 − 3 10^{-3} . Because no closed-form null is exact in practice, each detector’s threshold is the empirical 10 − 3 10^{-3} quantile of its p-values on 10,000 unwatermarked answers scored under 10 keys ( 10 5 10^{5} null p-values; calibration in Figure 9 ). Detection is measured on the first 100 or 200 tokens, with key-only (unweighted) scores unless stated otherwise. We generate 3000 answers per configuration on Qwen3.5-9B, with or without speculative decoding, and 1000 on the other models. Diversity is measured as in TextSeal, by Self-BLEU among answers to the same question under a fixed key (mean BLEU over all pairs of answers; lower is more diverse), on 100 questions with 32 answers each, or 16 under speculative decoding. Measuring diversity by the share of distinct 4-grams instead leaves the conclusions unchanged, except that textGrain is then slightly ahead of the copulas without speculative decoding ( Appendix F ).
To compare at equal diversity, each method’s detection is interpolated along its diversity–detection curve at TextSeal’s Self-BLEU; 95% intervals come from a bootstrap that resamples questions jointly across methods, so intervals for differences are paired.

blocks.en: 4.2 Without speculative decoding
blocks.zh: 4.2 (中文(简体) ). 没有投机解码

blocks.en:
Interpolated at TextSeal’s Self-BLEU, TextSeal2 detects 10, 22 and 8 percentage points more 100-token answers than the coin flip ( Sander et al., 2026 ) on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-27B respectively (paired 95% intervals [ + 4 , + 15 ] [+4,+15] , [ + 15 , + 25 ] [+15,+25] and [ + 3 , + 12 ] [+3,+12] ; Figure 1 a and Figure 7 ).
Against textGrain, TextSeal2 is ahead on Llama-3.1-8B ( + 11 +11 [ + 4 , + 17 ] [+4,+17] ), level on Qwen3.5-9B ( + 1 +1 [ − 5 , + 8 ] [-5,+8] ), and behind on Qwen3.5-27B ( − 5 -5 [ − 10 , 0 ] [-10,0] ).
AutoMark’s copula, which coincides with TextSeal2 in distribution, stays within 3 points throughout, confirming that the gain over TextSeal comes from removing the coin flip rather than from implementation differences.
With the public key alone, TextSeal2 still detects 27% / 67% of 100 / 200-token answers at ρ = 0.9 \rho=0.9 ; merging four keys detects as much as merging two, so extra keys cost nothing ( Appendix F ).

blocks.en: TextSeal’s entropy-weighted test improves every method by 4–23 points at 200 tokens, without changing the ranking ( Figure 5 , Table 6 ). On Qwen3.5-9B, TextSeal2 detects 78% / 97% of 100 / 200-token answers, against 74% / 97% for textGrain; under speculative decoding, 67% / 95%, against 48% / 87% for TextSeal and 36% / 76% for textGrain (Self-BLEU 18.9–20.1).

blocks.en: Under random word substitutions, TextSeal2 retains more detections than TextSeal and as many as textGrain, while paraphrasing by an LLM removes almost every watermark, as expected for token-level schemes ( Table 7 ). The gains over the coin flip persist at temperature 0.7 ( Appendix F ). TextSeal2’s decoding step is within 0.6% of TextSeal’s once key-only work overlaps the forward pass ( Table 5 ), and its post-logits work is one pass over the vocabulary ( Appendix D ).

blocks.en: On the 500 MBPP test problems ( Table 12 ), TextSeal2 detects 55% of answers at 256 tokens, against 39% / 46% / 50% for TextSeal/ textGrain / SynthID-Text (AutoMark’s copula: 59%). In long thinking traces (up to 2048 tokens; Table 13 ), 16% of positions on ELI5 and 34% on MBPP repeat an earlier window. There, continuing each window’s race from its leftovers instead of using it once detects 3.8 3.8 [ + 2.1 , + 5.6 ] [+2.1,+5.6] points more at 256 tokens on ELI5 and 7.6 7.6 [ + 2.4 , + 12.8 ] [+2.4,+12.8] points more at 512 tokens on MBPP, and raises median z-scores, without measurable distortion ( Table 13 ).

blocks.en: 4.3 With speculative decoding

blocks.en:

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
TextSeal2 satisfies the four requirements we set out for a deployed watermark: it is exactly distortion-free, preserves diversity under a fixed key, stays within 0.9% of plain sampling when key-only work overlaps the forward pass, and maintains the acceptance rate of speculative decoding.
Its detection is comparable to that of textGrain overall – ahead on Llama-3.1-8B, level on Qwen3.5-9B, and slightly behind on Qwen3.5-27B at 100 tokens – without textGrain’s per-token optimisation.
Our analysis attributes the previous gap to TextSeal’s coin-flip routing rather than to the absence of optimal transport: merging the two keys into one virtual key removes the 2 \sqrt{2} loss in signal-to-noise ratio, while still allowing one key to be published for public detection.
For speculative decoding, drawing the drafts by keyed races and choosing block verification’s outcome by a race on their leftovers carries the watermark without lowering acceptance.
blocks.zh:
TextSeal2 满足了我们为部署的水印设定的四个要求:它完全没有扭曲,在固定的钥匙下保持多样性,当只按键的工作与前传重叠时保持在0.9%的纯采样范围内,并保持了投机解码的接受率.
它的探测率与文本Grain整体相当 — — 在Llama-3.1-8B上领先,在Quen3.5-9B上位,在Quen3.5-27B上以100个符号略为落后 — — 没有文本Grain的平分优化。
我们的分析将之前的缺口归结为TextSeal的硬币-滑行路由而不是缺乏最佳的运输方式:将两把钥匙合并为一把虚拟钥匙可以去除信号-噪声比的2\sqrt{2}损失,同时仍然允许发布一把钥匙供公众检测.
对于投机解码,按键的种族绘制草稿,通过在所剩的地上进行比赛来选择区块核查的结果,背上水印而不会降低接受率。

blocks.en:
Our evaluation covers three domains (open-ended ELI5 answers, MBPP code, and AIME math problems under speculative decoding) and three open-weight models, at temperatures 0.7–1.
With block verification and 8 drafts, speculative decoding costs 2–4 percentage points of detection relative to standard decoding, and our speculative-decoding implementation is unbatched, so we do not measure wall-clock speedups.
We do not analyse attacks that exploit knowledge of the public key beyond the private verification it enables ( Milis et al., 2026 ) .
Finally, textGrain’s code is not public, so we use our reimplementation ( Appendix G ); its deployed parameters may differ.

blocks.en:
At generation, a key’s values at a given window serve at most one emitted token per answer, and a position whose window was already used draws its values afresh, which is plain sampling ( Appendix G ).
Under speculative decoding, a window counts as used once a round races it, whether or not its position is kept.
The positions after I I are discarded, but their keyed values still shaped the outcome: the relay reads the leftovers of every position, and ℙ ⁡ ( I = i ) \mathbb{P}(I=i) depends on the later drafts.
A position whose window was already raced, earlier in the text or earlier in the same round, therefore uses freshly drawn values, so the positions of a round have independent values.
A round races N + 1 N+1 windows but emits only I I tokens, so more positions fall back to fresh values than without speculative decoding.
Without speculative decoding, TextSeal2 can instead continue a window’s race at each later visit, as the ResidualRace of AutoMark does ( Gloaguen et al., 2026 ) : it keeps the leftovers of the window’s last race and gives the token that won it a freshly drawn exponential.
At detection, each (window, token) pair is scored once, at its first occurrence.

blocks.en:
Reusing a window’s keyed values re-runs the same race: each token still follows the model given its prefix, averaged over keys, but tokens at repeated windows become dependent, so the law of the whole answer is not the model’s.
Under the rules, each position reads keyed values that no earlier race has read, or freshly drawn values, which are independent of the prefix and of the randomness that produced it.
Each token then follows the model given its prefix, and the chain rule over positions gives the model’s law for the whole answer; under speculative decoding, this is part (iii) of Proposition 1 , whose proof uses exactly this independence.
With leftover continuation, given the earlier visits of a window, the leftovers of its losing tokens are again i.i.d. Exp ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathrm{Exp}(1) by Lemma 1 , and the winner’s fresh value is independent of them, so every visit is distortion-free given the  past.

In each round, Qwen3.5-0.8B proposes N N drafts, one at a time, from its own distribution (after temperature and top- p p ) through the scheme’s sampler; Qwen3.5-9B then evaluates p → 1 , … , p → N + 1 \vec{p}_{1},\dots,\vec{p}_{N+1} in a single forward pass, and the round emits the kept drafts and one more token, by block verification ( Sun et al., 2025 ) with the closed forms of Appendix A.3 .
A draft that is an end-of-sequence token ends the round’s drafting, so the round then has fewer than N N drafts.
TextSeal2 follows Algorithm 1 : drafts by the race ( 5 ), then the residual race ( 6 ), with the copula noise η \eta drawn once per position and read by both races.
The unwatermarked reference is native block verification with freshly drawn randomness. N = 8 N=8 is the main setting; Table 9 reports N = 4 N=4 and 16 16 , for which every configuration was generated again.
During generation, each answer tracks the (window, key) pairs whose values have been used, and every pair that a round reads counts as used,  kept or  not,  for  every  scheme  (Appendix A.5 ).
When a window has already been used, TextSeal and SynthID-Text fall back to their other key and then to fresh randomness, and textGrain and the copulas directly to fresh randomness (for TextSeal2, freshly drawn lane lengths, on which the draft race and the residual race still run).
Both models keep a key–value cache that is rolled back to the kept prefix after each round; on 40 random rounds, the logits after a rollback match a recomputation without cache as closely as those of a cache without rollback (bfloat16 noise).

blocks.en: The Self-BLEU of a question is the mean sentence-level BLEU (sacrebleu) over all ordered pairs of its answers generated under the fixed key, decoded from their first 200 tokens. This is TextSeal’s two-generation diversity estimator averaged over all answer pairs; we report the mean over questions. Intervals for values interpolated at TextSeal’s Self-BLEU resample the 100 questions jointly for all methods (and detection outcomes binomially within questions), so that question-level variation common to all methods cancels in paired comparisons. Figure 10 repeats Figure 1 with diversity measured by the share of distinct 4-grams among a question’s answers. The copulas still dominate the coin flip, and TextSeal2 still leads under speculative decoding; without speculative decoding, textGrain is slightly ahead of the copulas under this metric (66% vs. 62% detected at TextSeal’s distinct-4 level), whereas it is level with TextSeal2 under Self-BLEU.

blocks.en: Each generation job uses one H200 GPU. Our speculative-decoding implementation (Hugging Face models with a key–value cache) is unbatched and unoptimised: with N = 8 N=8 it takes about 0.11 s per token on one GPU, three times slower than plain decoding with the target, because the drafter is called once per draft; this affects only experimental throughput, not any reported rate, since block verification is exact. Under it, the residual race’s decision takes 0.33 ms per token, against 0.38 ms for native block verification, and computing the keyed lane lengths of the drafted positions takes 2.4 ms per token more than sampling the drafts without a key; this key-only work can run concurrently with the drafter’s forward pass ( Appendix D ).

The textGrain report ( Li et al., 2026 ) releases no code, so we implemented its Algorithms 1 and A.1 from the text: a keyed partition of the vocabulary into B = 256 B=256 blocks derived from the key and the window; a 256 × 256 256\times 256 table of standardised keyed Gumbel costs with m = 256 m=256 columns (the report fixes neither B B nor m m ); the log-domain Sinkhorn updates with marginal correction and the regularisation update of its Eq. (A.4); selection of a keyed column; and independent sampling of the block and then of the token within it. Detection follows its Section 3.2 ( Gamma ⁡ ( n , 1 ) \mathrm{Gamma}(n,1) null), except  that, as for every method in this  paper, we score the first occurrence of each (window, token) pair rather than each window’s first occurrence, which adds about 1% more scored positions.
We validated the GPU kernels against a direct (unoptimised) implementation of the algorithm on random inputs, and verified on toy distributions that the emitted-token distribution is unbiased and that the entropy removed respects the budget β \beta .
The speculative recipe implements its Appendix B with block verification between the watermarked distributions. OpenAI’s implementation and hyperparameters may differ from ours, and our textGrain numbers carry that caveat.

blocks.en:
Watermarks give providers, platforms and the public one signal for tracing AI-generated text. They are not robust to paraphrasing ( Table 7 ), can in principle be spoofed or removed by determined adversaries, and should therefore be combined with complementary provenance signals rather than treated as proof of origin.
Publishing a detection key enables independent public verification, but also gives adversaries a target signal to attack; retaining a private key allows such manipulation to be detected ( Milis et al., 2026 ) .

发布一个检测密钥可以独立进行公开核查,但也给对手一个目标信号来攻击;保留一个私人密钥可以探测出这种操纵(Milis等,2026年).
